title: Bucket Salaries Into Bands
description:
Bucket every employee into a salary band and count each band:

- `Low` — under 80000
- `Mid` — 80000 up to but not including 130000
- `High` — 130000 and above

Employees with a NULL salary belong to the band `Unknown`. Report only bands that contain at least one employee.

Name the columns `band` and `headcount`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT CASE
         WHEN salary IS NULL THEN 'Unknown'
         WHEN salary < 80000 THEN 'Low'
         WHEN salary < 130000 THEN 'Mid'
         ELSE 'High'
       END AS band,
       COUNT(*) AS headcount
FROM employees
GROUP BY band;
hint: CASE arms are evaluated top to bottom, so test the NULL case first and let the ranges fall through.
outputExplanation: Two employees are in the High band ($130k+), four in the Mid band ($80k–$130k), and two in the Low band (under $80k). No employee has a NULL salary in this dataset.
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE departments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  location TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  salary INTEGER,
  dept_id INTEGER,
  manager_id INTEGER,
  hire_date TEXT
);
